calAssistBuildData.purpose: Evidence-based roadmap of remaining product work, estimated completion, release blockers, and improvement recommendations. Percentages are planning estimates from a repository review and are not automated test coverage or a guarantee of feature completeness.

executiveSummary.estimatedOverallImplementation: Weighted estimate across backend foundations, planning engines, data persistence, frontend, integrations, testing, security and operations. The weighting and estimates are documented in the workstreams section.
executiveSummary.estimatedProductionReadiness: Development API and frontend routes have been observed running, but the complete production release path, user workflows, provider credentials, recovery procedures, and production security controls have not been verified end to end.
executiveSummary.currentState: CAL_ASSIST has a substantial NestJS and Prisma backend, planning and scheduling engines, a React frontend shell, health checks, and deployment scaffolding. The API type-check passed and the readiness endpoint reported a connected database in the latest check. The main remaining gap is turning backend capabilities into durable, tested, user-facing product workflows and a repeatable production release.

keyReleaseBlockers.blocker: Several frontend routes are explicit Coming soon pages; the calendar is a visual shell and key task actions are not wired.
Commitment risk and proactive intervention state are not persisted; commitment reminders and intervention mutations return 501.
Compatibility representations for permissions and autonomy policies should be replaced with explicit schema models and migrations.
CI deploy jobs contain placeholders, so a production deployment is not automated or proven.
Automated tests exist, but the checked-in test footprint is small relative to the product surface and there is no observed frontend test suite.

verificationSnapshot.check: Backend TypeScript check completed successfully after the compatibility changes.
API readiness endpoint returned ok and reported the database connected.
A production build passed before the final module-provider adjustment; the later watch process compiled with zero errors. Re-run the production build without a competing watch process.
Full unit, integration, browser, accessibility, security, and deployment acceptance suites.
No database migration or schema push was run; none is implied by this report.
External provider functionality depends on correctly configured credentials and real account-level verification.

workstreams.scoringMethod: Estimated current functional completion; weights sum to 100. Overall estimate is the weighted sum.

workstream.name: Backend foundation and domain APIs
workstream.evidence: API starts, health checks and database connectivity work; core NestJS modules and domain APIs are present. Build success does not prove every endpoint's behavior.

workstream.name: Planning, scheduling, reality and replanning
workstream.evidence: Time Compiler and multiple engine modules are documented and implemented. End-to-end product flows and broad regression coverage remain to be demonstrated.

workstream.name: Schema and durable feature persistence
workstream.evidence: Core Prisma entities exist, but schema gaps force reduced commitment behavior and compatibility storage for policy features.

workstream.name: Frontend product workflows
workstream.evidence: React shell, login, Today, Calendar, and Tasks routes exist. Goals, Projects, Commitments, Assistant, Insights, and Settings are currently Coming soon; some visible actions are not connected to mutations.

workstream.name: Calendar, AI and notification integrations
workstream.evidence: Provider adapters and interfaces are present, but credential setup, real OAuth/sync tests, delivery verification, and at least one Apple adapter placeholder remain.

workstream.name: Automated quality and regression coverage
workstream.evidence: Two backend unit spec files and one API end-to-end test file were found; there is no observed frontend test suite. Coverage and CI results need fresh verification.

workstream.name: Security, privacy and account safety
workstream.evidence: JWT authentication, permissions, validation and throttling are present in the codebase; production configuration, tenant isolation, secret handling, retention, and threat-model controls need explicit verification.

workstream.name: Production deployment and operations
workstream.evidence: Docker, Compose, monitoring configuration and CI scaffolding exist, but staging and production workflow steps are placeholders and no operational recovery acceptance was performed.

item.title: Complete the Prisma data model and safe migrations
item.why: Current compatibility code cannot durably represent all promised feature behavior. The checked-in Commitment schema does not store the full person, related-entity, confidence, reminder-policy, or risk data needed by the richer product design. Interventions are computed but not persisted.

tasks.task: Add explicit schema entities/fields for commitment metadata, risk assessments, reminder state, and proactive intervention lifecycle.
Give permissions, autonomy policies, rules, and rule-conflict resolutions first-class typed storage rather than overloading unrelated JSON/string fields.
Design a reviewed migration, backup/restore plan, and compatibility rollout; do not use schema push on production data.
Backfill or clearly handle existing rows, add indexes/uniqueness constraints, and test rollback or forward-recovery procedures.

item.acceptance: Migration deploys against a clean database and a copy of existing data; records survive restart; API contract and generated Prisma types agree; rollback/recovery is documented.
item.estimate: 1-2 engineering weeks, dependent on product decisions for retention and data semantics.

item.title: Finish the primary signed-in user workflows
item.why: The product shell routes users to several Coming soon views. Calendar currently renders an empty-state shell, and task creation/completion affordances are not fully connected to backend operations.

tasks.task: Implement Today as an accurate agenda with live data, real recommendations, useful empty/loading/error states, and no hard-coded recommendation content.
Connect Calendar to event APIs with month/week/day views, create/edit/delete, recurrence handling, conflict feedback, and timezone clarity.
Connect Tasks create, update, complete, delete, filters, due dates, and project/goal linking.
Replace Goals, Projects, Commitments, Assistant, Insights, and Settings Coming soon screens with MVP workflows or deliberately hide routes until complete.
Make mutations optimistic only when rollback/error handling is correct; show actionable errors instead of console-only logging.

item.acceptance: A new user can sign in, create a task and event, plan a day, make a change, refresh, and see the persisted result without developer tools.
item.estimate: 3-6 engineering weeks for an integrated MVP, depending on final design and scope.

item.title: Complete commitment risk, interventions and reminders
item.why: Risk is computed on demand; reminder sending returns 501; intervention acknowledgement, dismissal and snoozing return 501. This is an explicit product limitation in the current build.

tasks.task: Persist and recalculate commitment risk with a clear freshness policy and explainable factors.
Persist proactive intervention states and implement acknowledge, dismiss, and snooze with ownership checks and audit history.
Deliver reminders through configured channels with idempotency, retry limits, quiet hours, preferences, unsubscribe controls, and delivery status.
Expose these workflows in the Commitments UI and show honest unavailable/error states when channels are not configured.

item.acceptance: API and UI tests verify create/update/risk/intervention/reminder lifecycle, no duplicate notifications on retry, and no cross-user data access.
item.estimate: 2-4 engineering weeks plus provider account setup.

item.title: Validate and stabilize API request and response contracts
item.why: There are Zod input schemas in the codebase, while Nest's global ValidationPipe uses class-validator DTO metadata. Confirm every controller actually receives effective validation and response shapes match client assumptions.

tasks.task: Audit every controller for DTO/class-validator or explicit Zod parsing; reject malformed input with consistent 400 responses.
Normalize query-string booleans, numbers, dates, pagination, enums, and nested payloads.
Generate or maintain an OpenAPI contract and use shared typed API models in the client.
Verify error responses are stable, safe to display, and do not leak internals.

item.acceptance: Contract tests cover valid, invalid, boundary, and unauthorized requests for each shipped endpoint; client types compile against the documented contract.

item.title: Expand automated tests around user journeys and data safety

tasks.task: Add backend unit tests for auth, permissions, commitments, reminders, interventions, scheduling, integrations, and error cases.
Add API integration tests with a disposable database and Redis where required.
Add frontend component and end-to-end browser tests for login, task/event CRUD, scheduling, errors, and persistence after refresh.
Define coverage thresholds for critical services and make CI fail on regression.
Run tests against migrations and a clean install; add seed data that is safe and deterministic.

item.acceptance: CI runs build, type-check, lint, migration checks, API tests and browser smoke tests reliably from a clean checkout.
item.estimate: 2-4 engineering weeks, parallelizable with UI work.

item.title: Verify integrations with real providers and failure cases

tasks.task: Complete or remove the Apple Calendar placeholder; verify Google and Outlook OAuth callback, token refresh, disconnect, incremental sync, and conflict resolution.
Test inbound and outbound calendar sync for duplicate events, deleted events, timezones, daylight-saving changes, recurrence, and provider rate limits.
Verify AI provider selection, structured output validation, timeout/retry behavior, rate limits, usage controls, and fallback behavior using non-sensitive test data.
Exercise email, SMS, push, and in-app notification setup in sandbox accounts; document which channels are supported in the MVP.
Surface missing credentials and provider outages in Settings and health/diagnostic views.

item.acceptance: Each advertised provider passes a documented connection, sync/delivery, refresh, revoke, and failure-recovery checklist.
item.estimate: 2-4 engineering weeks plus provider approval/configuration time.

item.title: Harden production security and privacy

tasks.task: Perform a threat model and verify authorization/ownership checks on every user-scoped API and background job.
Require strong production secrets from a secret manager; remove unsafe fallback credentials and prevent secrets from appearing in logs or client bundles.
Review CORS, cookie/token storage, JWT expiry/rotation/revocation, password reset, session management, brute-force protection, and account recovery.
Add data export/deletion, retention rules, AI-provider data handling disclosures, and consent controls for calendar/email integrations.
Run dependency scanning, static analysis, security tests, and an external penetration review before broad launch.

item.acceptance: Production configuration fails closed for missing secrets; authorization tests prove tenant isolation; privacy policy, deletion/export behavior, and incident response are reviewed.

item.title: Make staging and production release repeatable
item.why: Docker and Compose scaffolding exist, but CI staging and production steps are placeholders. Local development success is not deployment readiness.

tasks.task: Choose and document the target hosting platform, environments, domains, TLS, networking, and managed PostgreSQL/Redis options.
Replace CI placeholder deploy steps with authenticated staging deployment, smoke tests, approval gates, and production promotion.
Run migrations as a controlled release step; define health checks, graceful shutdown, rollback, and version compatibility.
Configure database backups, restore drills, retention, Redis persistence expectations, and disaster recovery objectives.
Set up alerts for uptime, API errors, queue lag, failed calendar sync, AI-provider failures, and notification delivery.
Document environment variables without putting secrets in source control; rotate any credentials that may have been exposed.

item.acceptance: A tagged release can be deployed to staging and promoted to production using the runbook; health checks, restore test, alert delivery, and rollback are demonstrated.
item.estimate: 2-3 engineering weeks plus infrastructure and operations setup.

item.title: Improve usability, accessibility and performance

tasks.task: Complete responsive layouts and keyboard navigation; verify contrast, focus indicators, screen-reader names, and reduced-motion preferences.
Use consistent design tokens, loading skeletons, empty states, confirmations for destructive actions, and undo where safe.
Optimize large calendar and task lists with pagination/virtualization and avoid refetching or recalculating expensive plans unnecessarily.
Add localization and clear timezone/locale controls; verify dates around daylight-saving transitions.
Run usability sessions with representative users and prioritize issues by observed impact.

item.acceptance: Accessibility checks have no critical blockers, core views work at mobile and desktop sizes, and a usability test confirms users can complete the key flows.
item.estimate: Ongoing; reserve 1-3 engineering weeks for the initial launch-quality pass.

item.title: Align docs and support material with actual behavior

tasks.task: Update README and API docs to separate implemented, partially implemented, and planned features.
Document local setup, environment configuration, migrations, OAuth callback URLs, provider setup, troubleshooting, backup/restore, and deployment.
Publish a user guide for permissions, AI suggestions, calendar sync, data export/deletion, and notification controls.

item.acceptance: A new developer can set up a clean environment and a new user can understand supported features without relying on undocumented assumptions.

recommendedMilestones.milestone: Complete schema design and migration, API contract validation, primary task/calendar UI, commitment limitation decisions, and journey-level tests.
Verify OAuth and AI providers, notification delivery, data export/deletion, privacy controls, staging deployment, monitoring, and recovery drills.
Close security review findings, demonstrate production rollback and restore, meet accessibility and performance budgets, and finalize support/runbook ownership.

suggestion.theme: Make the product useful before adding more engines

improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Ship the Today, Calendar, Tasks, and Assistant loop end to end. Prioritize a dependable daily planning workflow over adding additional backend modules.

suggestion.theme: Explain AI and keep the user in control

improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Show why each recommendation was made, distinguish facts from inference, require confirmation for consequential changes, and provide undo and audit history.

suggestion.theme: Unify the data model and remove compatibility shortcuts

improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Treat Prisma schema, API validation, OpenAPI, and frontend types as one versioned contract. Add migrations only after review and test against existing data.
Replace console-only failures and generic empty states with clear recovery guidance for offline API, expired OAuth, missing AI credentials, and failed reminders.
Minimize stored calendar and AI-provider data, provide data export/deletion and consent controls, document retention, and keep secrets outside source code.

suggestion.theme: Measure outcomes rather than feature counts

improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Track schedule acceptance, completed planned tasks, avoided conflicts, reminder delivery, sync freshness, and user-reported trust. Use opt-in, privacy-preserving analytics.
Add dashboards and alerts for API health, database latency, queue backlog, provider failures, sync lag, and notification delivery; rehearse restore and rollback.

assumptionsAndLimitations.assumption: Percentages are engineering estimates from source files, project documentation, and the latest runtime/type-check evidence available at report creation.
Feature descriptions in CAL_UPDATE_INFO/PROGRESS.md may describe intended or implemented backend capability; they are not proof of production behavior unless supported by tests and runtime evidence.
Effort ranges assume one experienced full-stack engineer with normal review and access to required provider accounts; parallel work or scope changes will alter estimates.
assumptionsAndLimitations.limitation: This is a build roadmap, not a security audit, full code audit, legal review, or deployment certification.
Do not run a database migration, schema push, or credential rotation solely from this XML; review the target environment and obtain the appropriate approval first.
